title: Agent Skills vs MCP
question: Should an AI capability be an Agent Skill, an MCP server, or both?
verdict: Default to a Skill for reusable procedure and bundled context. Add MCP for live or dynamic tools and resources; combine them when the Skill should orchestrate an MCP-backed capability.

nodes.label: Current position
nodes.text: Choose by capability boundary, not by format popularity.

nodes.label: Use a Skill
nodes.text: Use an Agent Skill for reusable instructions, examples, references, assets, and scripts that should load only when a workflow is relevant.

nodes.label: Filesystem contract
nodes.text: The Agent Skills specification defines a SKILL.md package with optional scripts, references, assets, and progressive disclosure.

nodes.label: Client adoption
nodes.text: GitHub documents the open Agent Skills standard across Copilot cloud agent, code review, CLI, app, and agent modes in multiple IDEs.

nodes.label: Distribution still moving
nodes.text: The current well-known discovery proposal is still a draft because there is no standard way to ask what skills a domain publishes.

nodes.label: Use MCP
nodes.text: Use MCP when a host must discover and call live tools, read dynamic resources, or use prompts across a local or remote client-server boundary.

nodes.label: Protocol boundary
nodes.text: The current MCP architecture lets servers expose tools, resources, and prompts to clients.

nodes.label: Use both
nodes.text: Pair them when a portable Skill should teach the workflow while MCP supplies live data or actions.

nodes.label: Runtime counterpressure
nodes.text: MCP's official security guidance covers authorization-specific attack classes and mitigations that a remote capability must operate correctly.

nodes.label: Qualification
nodes.text: A Skill is not automatically static or safe: it may include executable scripts, and support for pre-approved tools varies by agent implementation.

nodes.label: Missing evidence
nodes.text: No committed cross-client benchmark yet measures whether one non-trivial Skill and one MCP integration behave consistently across major coding agents.

edges.note: The package format directly represents reusable procedure and on-demand supporting material.
A documented open format has a credible portability path beyond one chat session.
Portable authoring is further along than stable remote discovery and distribution.
MCP's primitives and transports are designed for live capability exchange.
A Skill can describe when and how to use tools that an MCP server exposes.
A live remote integration adds authorization and operational risk, so MCP should not be the default for static guidance.
Choosing a Skill changes the packaging boundary; it does not remove the need to review code and permissions.
Reusable procedure and bundled context fit the Skill boundary.
Live data and actions fit a protocol boundary.
The formats compose when a workflow needs both procedural knowledge and runtime capability.
A shared behavioral suite is needed before claiming equivalent portability in practice.
